nodes.lingshu_caption: The sagittal T2 weighted MRI shows a hyperintense signal at the C1-C2 level. This could represent edema or inflammation. The spinal cord appears to be intact without any obvious signs of compression or displacement. The vertebral bodies and intervertebral discs appear normal. There is no evidence of fractures or dislocations.

The spinal cord appears to be compressed at the level of C3-C4. The vertebral bodies appear to be intact without any obvious fractures or dislocations. There is no evidence of disc herniation or other abnormalities in the intervertebral discs. The surrounding soft tissues appear to be normal.

The sagittal STIR MRI image shows a hyperintense signal in the region of the cervical spine, specifically at the C2-C3 level. The hyperintensity suggests the presence of edema or inflammation. There is no evidence of spinal cord compression or significant stenosis. Surrounding soft tissues do not exhibit any abnormal signal changes.
